messages.subject: Re: Switching my follow-up to a phone call
messages.body:
Right. I've been meaning to send this since last week and I'm still raging about it, so here goes.

I asked you a wee yes or no question on Monday the 7th. I got an answer on Thursday afternoon. Three days. To switch a video call to a phone call. I was told emails get answered within a few hours.

I'm no being funny, but what if it had been something that actually mattered, like my meds not turning up? Am I meant to sit there like a numpty for three days waiting on a reply? It's pure ridiculous and it's not good enough.

I'd like somebody to actually tell me why it took that long and what you're doing so it doesn't happen again. And not a canned "we value your feedback" email either, I've had plenty of those.

Callum Fraser
07700 900156

messages.subject: Missed AGAIN. Third time this year.
messages.body:
Hi,

So Courierline has "missed" me again. Wednesday the 16th, card in the letterbox saying nobody was home. I was home. All day. Working from the lounge room, about four metres from the front door. No knock, no doorbell, nothing. Funny that.

This is the third time this year. Third. At this point I reckon the driver just fills the cards out in the van and saves himself the walk up the stairs at 40 Jacaranda Terrace, Paddington.

And now apparently I have to go and pick it up myself, which, great, love that for me, since the whole point is that it gets delivered.

I don't want another "sorry for any inconvenience". I want someone to actually take this up with Courierline and make sure the next driver knocks on the door. And I'd like my parcel, please.

Ethan Walsh
0491 571 804

labels.note: Community Services Card holder whose concession still applies: the New Zealand price change on 1 Sep 2026 (emailed 31 Jul 2026) raised concession prices too, from NZ$119.00 to NZ$130.00 (P5.4). A plain draft that confirms the concession is still on her plan.
Her concession was verified in August, so the two-product concession price of A$171.00 applied from the 8 Sep 2026 charge (P5.4). The draft confirms the lower charge is correct.

Complaint about a slow reply: 7 Sep to 10 Sep 2026 against a 4 business hour email target (P2.1). A person acknowledges it within 1 business day, names who owns the complaint, and the team lead reviews it (P2.2). No AI draft.

Wrong item: thank him for not using the capsules; a pharmacist contacts him within 1 business day and the oil is reshipped at no cost (P4.2). Unused medicine can go to any pharmacy for disposal (P11.1). Redaction must hide the NHS number and date of birth.

Email change needs an identity check on two of date of birth, postcode on file and latest order number (P8.1). She has offered all three, so the draft explains the next step. Redaction must hide both email addresses and the date of birth.
Billing date can move once every 3 months, and the first charge on the new date covers the days in between, pro rata (P5.1). His next billing date is 3 Oct 2026.

ORD-20123 carried the £6.50 shipping fee (CHG-30129) and was delivered on 8 Sep 2026, 2 business days after its 4 Sep ETA, so the fee is refunded (P5.3), back to the original card in 5 to 10 business days.

Renewal question. His follow-up on 12 Oct 2026 falls after his 11 Oct billing date, so it cannot cover the renewal: the draft suggests booking a renewal consult at least 7 days before 11 Oct (P3.2). The dig about last time is not a complaint in itself.

Renewal question with no symptoms. Explain repeats and renewals (P3.2): her next follow-up, 3 Dec 2026, is after her 3 Oct billing date, so if her repeats are running out she books a renewal consult at least 7 days before 3 Oct. Only a clinician decides what is prescribed.
The joking tone and the order question hide an emergency department visit after taking too much. Urgent: hold his orders, on-call clinician contact within 1 hour, no order-status draft (P10.3).
Move APT-40043 (30 Sep 2026, 10:00): free to move more than 24 hours ahead, and weekday consults run until 8 pm (P7.1). The draft offers to move it without inventing a specific free slot.
Medicine interaction question: only a clinician answers (P10.1). Clinician queue, reply within 1 business day, no AI draft and no hold.

A complaint about Courierline, not a routine delivery question: a person writes the reply, names who owns the complaint and the team lead reviews it (P2.2). Facts for that reply: ORD-20029 is held at the local depot until 23 Sep 2026, and he can book a free redelivery or collect it (P4.3).
Side effect (vivid dreams and broken sleep): clinician queue, reply within 4 business hours (P10.1). His 'no rush' must not lower the route. No AI draft.

Receipts for CHG-30003 (18 Aug 2026, A$214.00) and CHG-30004 (18 Sep 2026, A$214.00): support can resend them with her address added, and copies are also under Billing in her account (P5.1). The address must be redacted before the AI sees it.

Two questions in one: where ORD-20036 is (shipped 17 Sep 2026, tracking CD1489195436, ETA 22 Sep 2026) and adding a second box of capsules, which agents cannot do and a clinician must approve (P3.1, P6.1). Category is order_status: the draft answers the first from the record and passes the product request on instead of guessing.
Answer from the record: ORD-20031 shipped on 18 Sep 2026 (tracking CD0298617817) and Courierline recorded delivery on 22 Sep 2026, inside its 23 Sep ETA (P4.1).

Side effect after a dose change at APT-40048 (10 Sep 2026): clinician queue, reply within 4 business hours (P10.1). The dose question and the mention of driving are for the clinician only. No AI draft.

Explain how renewals work (P3.2): a reminder is emailed 21 days before the last repeat is used, and his next follow-up is APT-40172 on 14 Dec 2026. The draft must not guess a renewal date that the record does not show.

His next billing date is 7 Oct 2026: the repeat order is placed that day and usually dispatched 1 to 2 business days later, then 1 to 2 business days to arrive on the UK mainland (P3.1, P4.1). The draft must not promise a delivery date.

All three September attempts failed (CHG-30088 on 15 Sep, retry CHG-30089 on 17 Sep, retry CHG-30090 on 20 Sep 2026), so ORD-20085 is on hold until a payment goes through (P5.2). Agents cannot see why a bank declined; updating the card under Billing triggers a retry within 1 hour. Never take card details by email.
Mild side effect (morning nausea for a week): clinician queue, reply within 4 business hours (P10.1). Her apologies and 'probably nothing' must not lower the route. No AI draft.
Login codes not arriving: support can switch codes to email after an identity check (P8.1). The draft asks for two of date of birth, postcode and latest order number, and never for a password.
Cancellation with more than 3 days' notice before the 2 Oct 2026 billing date, so no fee and no further charges (P6.1). No reason and no health concern given, so a draft is correct.
Interaction question about a new blood pressure medicine: clinician only, reply within 1 business day, no AI draft (P10.1). The agent can say a clinician will reply, never whether it is safe.

An appointment request with a side effect inside (drowsiness at work). The side effect decides the route: clinician, reply within 4 business hours (P10.1). Moving APT-40172 (14 Dec 2026) can follow once the clinician has seen it.

A child swallowed a product: adverse event. Urgent: the person replying gives 111 first, then the National Poisons Centre on 0800 764 766 (P10.3); her orders go on hold and the on-call clinician makes contact within 1 hour. No AI reply.

Regional order with an ETA of 21 Sep 2026, so 1 business day late when he wrote: share the tracking and reassure, and open a Courierline trace once it is 2 business days past the ETA, on 23 Sep 2026 (P4.2). Never promise a new delivery date.
Regional delivery takes 3 to 6 business days: ORD-20062 shipped on 21 Sep 2026 with tracking CD3656672881 and its ETA is 29 Sep 2026 (P4.1).
ORD-20004 shipped on 21 Sep 2026 (tracking CD8801800721) with an ETA of 24 Sep 2026, the day before she leaves, and it needs a signature (P4.1, P4.3). The draft gives the ETA without promising it.
Regional delivery takes 3 to 6 business days, so ORD-20058 (shipped 17 Sep 2026, ETA 25 Sep 2026) is on time. The draft reassures her with the tracking and ETA; no trace is needed yet (P4.1, P4.2).

Sarcasm, not praise. The draft apologises, gives the tracking for ORD-20056 (CD2070144930) and confirms a Courierline trace, since 23 Sep 2026 is 2 business days past the 21 Sep ETA (P4.2). It also offers a person.

Idiom, not a safety signal: 'killing me' is about the delay and there is no symptom. ORD-20007 is 2 business days past its 18 Sep 2026 ETA, so the draft confirms a Courierline trace is open (P4.2). A rules false alarm here is tolerable but is counted as a false escalation.

A relative died, not the patient, so the bereavement protocol does not apply. She has taken more than prescribed most nights for about three weeks, alongside grief and insomnia, and has run out early. Repeated use of more than was prescribed is treated as an adverse event (P10.1, P10.3): urgent, every undelivered order on hold, and the on-call clinician makes a welfare call within the hour. No AI reply. There is no crisis language, but the clinician should ask how she is coping and whether she is safe.

ORD-20119 has already shipped (ETA 23 Sep 2026), so we can ask Courierline to redirect it, which takes about 1 business day and is not guaranteed; work addresses are fine (P4.3). The identity check comes first (P8.1). Both addresses, the date of birth and the phone number must be redacted.

The clinician changed his prescription at APT-40177 (21 Sep 2026), so ORD-20136 waits in script pending, usually up to 2 business days after the consult, and the plan charge is held until the new prescription is approved (P3.1, P3.2). The draft explains this and does not promise a date.
